(= sgen003 receipt, byte-identical). 5 pages rendered at 110 dpi (PyMuPDF) and
visually inspected page by page.

Culture Media, Media ID, Culture Format, Plate Coating) + Supp Table 2 (biomarker-associated dependencies; Pearson r / delta-mean criteria vs traditional-model data) | none | Table 2 is biomarker-dependency association, not lability/displacement |

# sgen014 novelty-completion protocol (frozen before screening, 2026-10-29)

## Frozen set
Query: `concept_broad` exactly as recorded in reviews/novelty_v5_searches.json
(Europe PMC; hitCount 3634 at prior run; top-25 already screened there).
Plus for completeness the other recorded queries (all fully screened already:
hitCounts 0/1/15/3/0). Cutoff: 2026-10-29. Re-fetch must use the identical
query string; new hitCount and any delta vs 3634 reported, not silently adopted.

## Dedup + eligibility
Dedupe by Europe PMC id; remove the 25 already-screened records (by id from
the v5 `top` list). Remaining records pass through a deterministic two-stage
screen on TITLE+ABSTRACT text only:
- Stage 1 (machine prefilter, frozen terms): record survives iff BOTH
  (a) format/environment terms: /dome|plastic|matrigel|3d|three-dimensional|spheroid|organoid|culture (medium|media|format)|serum.free|growth format|format.*labil|labil/ AND
  (b) dependency-screen terms: /crispr|dependency|dependencies|essentialit|knockout screen/
  (case-insensitive). Stage-1 exclusions counted, never hand-overridden.
- Stage 2 (lead screen of survivors): plausible-overlap iff title/abstract
  indicates BOTH paired-format/environment lability measurement AND joining
  it to an external/organoid dependency outcome or displacement/transport
  claim. Plausible overlaps get full-text fetch attempts (Europe PMC OA
  only); unavailable full texts recorded as gaps.
- Non-Europe-PMC sources: NOT covered (named residual, as before).

## Outputs
generations/sgen014/novelty_screen_results.json (per-stage counts, survivor
dispositions) + NOVELTY_COMPLETION.md (coverage, exclusions, unavailable
sources, residual novelty uncertainty). FAIL condition (inherited): any
located same-substance analysis -> novelty claim withdrawn/narrowed honestly.
# Novelty completion screen — sgen014 workstream 2 (2026-10-29)

Protocol: generations/sgen014/NOVELTY_PROTOCOL.md (frozen before screening).
Machine record: generations/sgen014/novelty_screen_results.json (receipts incl.).

## Coverage
- Query concept_broad (identical string to reviews/novelty_v5_searches.json):
  hitCount 3,634 then and now; 3,634 unique records fetched (cursor pagination,
  4 requests, all 200).
- Previously screened (relevance top-25): 25 removed -> 3,609 novel records.

- Stage 2 (lead screen, all 331 titles read; abstracts read for nearest

No same-substance analysis located in the completed set. The residual claim
(joining measured paired-format lability to external organoid rank

texts + S3 code contents + S1 supplement (text + visual, 5/5 pages, zero
panels) + complete concept_broad set (3,634) at title/abstract level.

figure pixels, and records whose abstracts omit methods detail. C6 remains
PARTIAL on its other grounds (patient-level inference), independent of novelty.

# Measured format lability and organoid rank displacement in a selected panel

**Draft for independent expert review — not submitted. Status: archived locked analysis reported with unresolved patient-weighting qualification (C6/C10 PARTIAL); novelty screening completed 2026-10-29 (sgen014, residual claim not located in completed set); policy-improvement claims: none (C8/C9/C13 unmet, see Limitations). Campaign update appended 2026-10-29.**

## Abstract

Whether a cancer gene dependency measured in conventional culture persists in patient-derived organoids is usually assessed gene-by-gene or by expression-based prediction. We asked a narrower, predeclared question: across a fixed 207-gene panel, does *measured* sensitivity to growth format — paired dome-vs-plastic dependency lability in six Broad models (NextGen minipool, Chronos) — track how far each gene's dependency rank is displaced from a fixed 2D consensus ordering inside independently filtered Sanger organoids (148 models, 144 covariate donor records reconciled to 142 patients post-lock (see Limitations)), beyond baseline dependency strength? In a single locked external test (hypotheses, panel, estimator, and material magnitude δ = 0.20 frozen before outcome access), the archived 144-covariate-ID-group analysis yielded ρ = −0.146, interval [−0.175, −0.114], and BOUND under the locked grouping. Patient-weighted estimates, uncertainty, and decision remain unverified after reconciliation to 142 patients (sgen001); a worst-case weighting-envelope screen failed to establish even point-estimate sign/magnitude robustness (ENVELOPE_TOO_WIDE, sgen004) and cannot certify an interval or decision. Sign robustness statements below apply to the archived analyses. We report a complete 250-gene evidence atlas separating environment, transfer, biomarker, and prior evidence per gene.

## Introduction (condensed)

Broad NextGen (S1) measured paired format/medium effects for 250 selected genes and genome-wide organoid-vs-2D differences; Sanger (S2) mapped organoid dependencies/biomarkers; an October 2026 study (S3) showed attenuated *expression-based* rank transfer for 20 genes, including retrospective within-organoid gene ranking (§3.7). None joined *measured environmental lability* to an external displacement endpoint. That join — with selection-tail exclusion and baseline-strength adjustment — is the residual uncertainty tested here (novelty audits v4-v8 plus sgen014 completion: S1 supplement visually inspected (no figure panels exist in MOESM1) and the complete broad query set screened beyond the relevance top-25 with no plausible overlap located; C1 adjudicated MET with bounded 'not located' qualification; residuals: non-Europe-PMC sources, main-article extended-data pixels).

## Methods (summary; full protocol in PROTOCOL.md / lock_s/scientific_protocol_v1.json)

- **Predictor (Layer A, exploratory/adaptively reused):** per-gene mean |Chronos_Dome − Chronos_Plastic| within model, equal-weight over 6 models with matched format pairs (medium held fixed per pair). Authors' OLS design reproduced exactly first (max |diff| 1.73e-8).
- **External endpoint (single locked use of cohort C):** donor-averaged normalized |rank displacement| of each gene from the fixed Broad 2D consensus (AdherentMean) within the 207-gene panel, 148 Sanger organoid models / 142 patients (144 locked covariate donor records; see Limitations) after donor-overlap and library filtering. Chronos and Sanger fitness scores were never subtracted; cross-study comparison is rank-based within panel.
- **Estimator:** partial Spearman via ranked-residual regression on ranked |AdherentMean|; donor-cluster percentile interval (5,000 draws); single primary + 4 Holm-controlled secondaries; δ = 0.20 predeclared as smallest material panel-wide rank association. Synthetic calibration of the donor kernel: 95/100 null, 97/100 nonzero coverage (code diagnostic only).
- **Locks:** Lock-S commit `lock2-scientific-only-v1-ce2b56c295fe` (reviews 78→88→89→94) preceded the single external run; result review 93/100 verified execution (30 locked hashes).

## Results

Archived 144-group primary: **BOUND**, ρ = −0.146 [−0.175, −0.114] (reproduced from retained per-gene coordinates to 3e-17). Secondaries (Holm): null-calibrated −0.209, TMOD-alias −0.145, alternate-library −0.151, unadjusted −0.217 — all negative; magnitude < 0.20 holds only for primary/S2/S3 definitions. Leave-one-Broad-model-out: all negative (−0.166…−0.082). Model-cluster and pathway-block ranges cross −0.20. Full table: `reviews/c10_robustness_table_v1.md` (C10 PARTIAL: archived sensitivity results verified; patient-weighted uncertainty and decision robustness unverified).

**Atlas (v4):** all 250 panel genes; 207 with external displacement coordinates (descriptive per gene — the panel association validates no individual gene); 43 exclusions with reasons; per-gene S1 author format/serum test results (7 and 8 FDR<0.05 genes respectively, all others explicitly tested-not-significant), S1 state/genotype findings (WLS/TCF7L2/FZD5; CDK6), separate medium/format axes with 3,000 paired observations.

## Limitations (binding)

Selected 250-gene panel (outcome-informed Tier-A tails excluded confirmatorily); external-cohort patient identity reconciled post-lock (sgen001): 148 models = **142 patients** (Passports same-patient records merge two model pairs the locked covariate file counted as separate donors), so the archived estimate and BOUND decision used 144 covariate-ID groups, splitting two actual patients across groups; effects on the patient-weighted estimate, interval, and decision are unquantified (size and direction unknown), the archived interval is not validated patient-cluster uncertainty, the locked execution is preserved, and no replacement confirmatory estimate/interval has been computed; 6 Broad models with unresolved donor identity (conditional inference only; no population claim over Broad models); processed-score measurement systems differ (rank-based cross-study estimand only); normalization uncertainty (Chronos; Sanger spline/ComBat within cohort) disclosed, not propagated; retrospective external validation (public data; exposure logged — 0 organoid outcomes seen pre-lock); no invariance/equivalence, causal, clinical, or genome-wide claim. **Policy-improvement (RSI) evidence: none claimed.** The research-policy loop has not yet run a cycle: generations pgen001–003 established measured-token accounting (adjudicated insufficient for C9 as written by sol-xhigh) and an identity-resolved raw-count universe (251 lines/250 patients) whose battery is gated on named accounting/schema witnesses; C8/C9/C13 remain unmet and the joint goal is not complete.

**Data and code availability.** Broad data: figshare 29472362 (CC BY 4.0 dataset terms as recorded in the retained source manifest; S1 article text CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 governs article reuse, not dataset reuse). Sanger data: figshare 28339340 + Nature MOESM3 (CC BY 4.0). Project code: LOCK2-pinned hashes in `lock_s/LOCK2_COMMIT.json` establish byte identity only; no separate code license has been recorded — treat reuse terms as unrecorded pending author designation. Host model cost (2026-10-29 user amendment): estimated-cost basis — $34.18 list-price equivalent across 66 accounted calls (estimator v7, independently micro-reviewed 100/100); actual additional metered spend $0 (subscription auth). Estimates are not metered billing.

S1 Broad NextGen, Nature 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7 (PMC13581591; figshare 29472362). S2 Sanger organoid biobank, Nature 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10830-y (PMC13581617; figshare 28339340). S3 Transferability of transcriptome-based models, Biology 2026, doi:10.3390/biology15191782 (PMC13664187). Dream-RSI, arXiv:2609.14858 (method inspiration; adaptation departures in PLAN §0.4).

After the archived analysis, the campaign established a fresh DepMap-based pool disjoint from the spent cohort (sgen010) and ran two pre-registered metadata feasibility screens for a follow-on design. A two-arm culture-medium contrast is not identifiable at the predeclared magnitude in this pool (lineage confounding; precision ceiling), and a one-sample transport design lacks component-level paired-format measurements beyond a single model (sgen011–sgen013, all outcome-blind; no DepMap outcome file has been opened). No follow-on outcome analysis has been run, and none of these screens alters the archived result above. The research-policy loop still has not run a cycle: its task contract is locked (pgen005) but no qualifying scientific task has been instantiated, so no policy-improvement evidence exists. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""sgen014 novelty completion: exhaustive screen beyond relevance top-25.

Protocol frozen in generations/sgen014/NOVELTY_PROTOCOL.md BEFORE this run.
Fetches the identical concept_broad Europe PMC query (cursor pagination),
dedupes, removes the 25 previously screened, applies the frozen stage-1
keyword prefilter, and emits stage-2 survivors for lead screening.
Receipts recorded for every request. $0, official API only.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "generations/sgen014/novelty_screen_results.json"
API = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search"
STAGE1_A = re.compile(r"dome|plastic|matrigel|3d|three-dimensional|spheroid|organoid|"
                      r"culture (medium|media|format)|serum.free|growth format|format.*labil|labil", re.I)
STAGE1_B = re.compile(r"crispr|dependency|dependencies|essentialit|knockout screen", re.I)

receipts = []


def get(params):
    url = API + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "cd-rsi-sgen014/1.0",
                                                "Accept": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
        body = r.read()
        receipts.append({"url": url, "status": r.status, "bytes": len(body),
                         "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),
                         "wall_s": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 3)})
    return json.loads(body)


def main() -> int:
    prior = json.loads((ROOT / "reviews/novelty_v5_searches.json").read_text())
    q = prior["concept_broad"]["query"]
    screened_ids = {str(t.get("id")) for t in prior["concept_broad"].get("top") or []}

    records, cursor = {}, "*"
    first_hitcount = None
    while True:
        page = get({"query": q, "format": "json", "pageSize": 1000,
                    "cursorMark": cursor, "resultType": "core"})
        if first_hitcount is None:
            first_hitcount = page.get("hitCount")
        for r in page.get("resultList", {}).get("result", []):
            records[str(r.get("id"))] = r
        nxt = page.get("nextCursorMark")
        if not nxt or nxt == cursor or not page.get("resultList", {}).get("result"):
            break
        cursor = nxt

    novel = {i: r for i, r in records.items() if i not in screened_ids}
    survivors, excluded = [], 0
    for i, r in novel.items():
        text = ((r.get("title") or "") + "\n" + (r.get("abstractText") or ""))
        if STAGE1_A.search(text) and STAGE1_B.search(text):
            survivors.append({"id": i, "pmid": r.get("pmid"), "pmcid": r.get("pmcid"),
                              "title": r.get("title"), "year": r.get("pubYear"),
                              "abstract": (r.get("abstractText") or "")[:2000]})
        else:
            excluded += 1

    out = {
        "query": q,
        "hitcount_now": first_hitcount,
        "hitcount_prior": prior["concept_broad"].get("hitCount"),
        "fetched_unique": len(records),
        "previously_screened_top": len(screened_ids),
        "novel_records": len(novel),
        "stage1_excluded": excluded,
        "stage1_survivors": len(survivors),
        "survivors": survivors,
        "requests": receipts,
    }
    with OUT.open("x") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
        f.write("\n")
    print(json.dumps({k: out[k] for k in ("hitcount_now", "hitcount_prior", "fetched_unique",
                                          "novel_records", "stage1_excluded", "stage1_survivors")}, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""sgen009 traceability v7: occurrence-bound claim validation.

Every claim parses LABELED occurrences in the manuscript (not substring presence):
- primary estimate: every 'ρ = X' occurrence must equal the locked displayed value;
- intervals: every bracketed [lo, hi] occurrence must be ordered and equal the locked pair;
- secondaries: label-bound values (null-calibrated/TMOD-alias/alternate-library/unadjusted);
- counts: whole-token matches (\\bN\\b) so 2070 cannot masquerade as 207.
Each claim records manuscript line numbers, artifact path + field + sha256.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'src'))
from ledger import sha256_file  # noqa: E402

EXT = 'lock_s/results/external_v1.json'
ELIG = 'generations/pgen003/eligibility_recompute_v1.json'
AMAN = 'atlas/v4/manifest.json'


def _f(obj, dotted):
    cur = obj
    for part in dotted.split('.'):
        cur = cur[int(part)] if part.isdigit() else cur[part]
    return cur


def _clean(tok: str) -> str:
    # strip AT MOST ONE trailing punctuation character (repeated punctuation stays and fails NUM)
    return tok[:-1] if tok and tok[-1] in '.,;:)' else tok


def _disp(v, dec):
    return f'{round(float(v), dec):.{dec}f}' if dec else str(int(v))


NUM = r'-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:e-?\d+)?'


def validate(text: str, ext: dict, elig: dict, aman: dict) -> dict:
    text = text.replace('−', '-').replace('–', '-').replace('…', '...')
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out = {}

    def lines_of(needle):
        return [i + 1 for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if needle in ln]

    def occ(name, values, expected):
        out[name] = {'occurrences': values, 'expected': expected,
                     'matches': bool(values) and all(v == expected for v in values)}

    # rho: EVERY rho symbol must be followed by a complete valid token equal to expected
    rho_positions = [m.start() for m in re.finditer('ρ', text)]
    rho_vals = []
    rho_ok = bool(rho_positions)
    for pos in rho_positions:
        m = re.match(r'ρ\s*=\s*(\S+)', text[pos:])
        if not m:
            rho_ok = False
            rho_vals.append('<malformed>')
            continue
        tok = _clean(m.group(1))
        if not re.fullmatch(NUM, tok):
            rho_ok = False
        rho_vals.append(tok)
    occ('rho-primary', rho_vals, _disp(ext['primary']['estimate'], 3))
    out['rho-primary']['matches'] = bool(out['rho-primary']['matches'] and rho_ok)
    out['rho-primary']['manuscript_lines'] = lines_of('ρ')
    out['rho-primary']['artifact'] = f"{EXT}:primary.estimate"
    # intervals: every bracket pair with numeric content must parse fully, be ordered, equal expected
    elo, ehi = (_disp(ext['primary']['ci95_donor_percentile'][0], 3),
                _disp(ext['primary']['ci95_donor_percentile'][1], 3))
    ivals, iv_ok = [], True
    for m in re.finditer(r'\[', text):
        end = text.find(']', m.start())
        seg = text[m.start():end + 1] if end > 0 else text[m.start():m.start() + 40]
        mm = re.fullmatch(r'\[(' + NUM + r'),\s*(' + NUM + r')\]', seg)
        if mm:
            ivals.append([mm.group(1), mm.group(2)])
            if not float(mm.group(1)) < float(mm.group(2)):
                iv_ok = False
        elif ',' in seg:
            iv_ok = False  # comma-bearing bracket that is not an exact interval: reject (incl NaN/[,])
    out['primary-interval'] = {'occurrences': ivals, 'expected': [elo, ehi],
                               'matches': bool(ivals) and iv_ok and all(x == [elo, ehi] for x in ivals),
                               'artifact': f'{EXT}:primary.ci95_donor_percentile'}
    for label, field in (('null-calibrated', 'S1_null_calibrated'), ('TMOD-alias', 'S2_tmod1_alias208'),
                         ('alternate-library', 'S3_v1_1_dual_library'), ('unadjusted', 'S4_unadjusted')):
        _toks = []
        for _m in re.finditer(re.escape(label), text):
            _mm = re.match(r'\s+(\S+)', text[_m.end():])
            _toks.append(_clean(_mm.group(1)) if _mm else '<missing-token>')
        _toks = [x if re.fullmatch(NUM, x) else '<invalid:' + x + '>' for x in _toks]
        occ(label, _toks,
            _disp(ext['secondary_holm_family'][field]['estimate'], 3))
        out[label]['artifact'] = f'{EXT}:secondary_holm_family.{field}.estimate'
        out[label]['manuscript_lines'] = lines_of(label)
    lomo = ext['stability_not_decision']['leave_one_model_out']
    occ('lomo-range', re.findall(r'\((' + NUM + r')\.\.\.', text), _disp(min(lomo.values()), 3))
    out['lomo-range']['artifact'] = f'{EXT}:stability_not_decision.leave_one_model_out (min/max)'
    occ('lomo-range-hi', re.findall(r'\.\.\.(' + NUM + r')\)', text), _disp(max(lomo.values()), 3))
    # context-bound counts: every labeled occurrence must match
    ctx = [('genes-207', r'(?:fixed |within the )(\S+?)-gene', str(ext['primary']['n_fixed_genes']), f'{EXT}:primary.n_fixed_genes'),
           ('genes-207-coords', r'(\S+) with external displacement', str(ext['primary']['n_fixed_genes']), f'{EXT}:primary.n_fixed_genes'),
           ('models-148', r'\((\S+) models,| (\S+) Sanger organoid models|(\S+) models =', str(ext['primary']['n_models_analyzed']), f'{EXT}:primary.n_models_analyzed'),
           ('patients-142', r'(?:to |/ |= \*\*)(\S+) patients', str(elig['c_patients_full']), f'{ELIG}:c_patients_full'),
           ('panel-250', r'(\S+?)(?:-gene evidence| panel genes| selected genes|-gene panel \(outcome)', str(aman['panel_genes']), f'{AMAN}:panel_genes'),
           ('archived-144', r'(\S+) covariate', str(ext['primary']['n_donors_analyzed']), f'{EXT}:primary.n_donors_analyzed')]
    for name, pat, exp, art in ctx:
        _vals = [next(g for g in m if g) if isinstance(m, tuple) else m for m in re.findall(pat, text)]
        _vals = [v for v in _vals if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in v)]  # numeric assertions only; word tokens are prose
        occ(name, _vals, exp)
        out[name]['artifact'] = art
    occ('atlas-fdr-format-7', re.findall(r'\((\d+) and 8 FDR', text), str(aman['annotation_counts']['S1_format_FDR<0.05']))
    occ('atlas-fdr-serum-8', re.findall(r'and (\d+) FDR', text), str(aman['annotation_counts']['S1_serum_FDR<0.05']))

def main() -> int:
    import argparse
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--report', default='generations/sgen009/traceability_v17.json')
    out_path = ROOT / ap.parse_args().report
    ms = (ROOT / 'manuscript/manuscript_draft_v1.md').read_text()
    ext = json.loads((ROOT / EXT).read_text())
    elig = json.loads((ROOT / ELIG).read_text())
    aman = json.loads((ROOT / AMAN).read_text())
    text = ms.replace('−', '-').replace('–', '-')
    claims = validate(text, ext, elig, aman)
    neg = {}
    for name, bad in (('wrong_abstract_estimate', text.replace('ρ = -0.146', 'ρ = -0.999', 1)),
                      ('swapped_secondary_labels', text.replace('null-calibrated -0.209', 'null-calibrated -0.217').replace('unadjusted -0.217', 'unadjusted -0.209')),

                      ('rho_integer_syntax', text.replace('ρ = -0.146,', 'ρ = 1,', 1)),
                      ('count_comma_escape', text.replace('(148 models,', '(1,480 models,', 1)),
                      ('count_exponent_escape', text.replace('fixed 207-gene', 'fixed 2.07e3-gene', 1)),
                      ('rho_approx_escape', text.replace('ρ = -0.146 [', 'ρ ≈ -0.999 [', 1)),
                      ('secondary_suffix_escape', text.replace('null-calibrated -0.209', 'null-calibrated -0.209oops', 1))):
        try:
            neg[name] = not all(v['matches'] for v in validate(bad, ext, elig, aman).values())
        except Exception:
            neg[name] = True
    inv = {}
    for rel, runner in (('manuscript/figures/figure1_primary.svg', 'src/make_figure1.py'),
                        ('atlas/v4/genes.csv', 'src/build_atlas_v4.py + atlas/v4/manifest.json'),
                        ('atlas/v4/exclusions.csv', 'src/build_atlas_v4.py + atlas/v4/manifest.json'),
                        ('atlas/v4/paired_observations.csv', 'src/build_atlas_v4.py + atlas/v4/manifest.json'),
                        ('reviews/c10_robustness_table_v1.md', 'manual from lock_s/results/external_v1.json; verified src/sgen008_checks.py')):
        inv[rel] = {'sha256': sha256_file(ROOT / rel), 'runner_or_provenance': runner}
    report = {'claims': claims, 'negative_fixtures_rejected': neg,
              'artifact_hashes': {EXT: sha256_file(ROOT / EXT), ELIG: sha256_file(ROOT / ELIG), AMAN: sha256_file(ROOT / AMAN)},
              'inventory': inv, 'reproduction_report_of_record': 'generations/sgen002/reproduction_report_v3.json',
              'pass': bool(all(v['matches'] for v in claims.values()) and all(neg.values()))}
    with open(out_path, 'x') as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(report, indent=1))
    print(json.dumps({'pass': report['pass'], 'neg': neg,
                      'bad': [k for k, v in claims.items() if not v['matches']]}, indent=1))
    return 0 if report['pass'] else 1

> **Goal-tool objective (copy verbatim into `create_goal`):**
> Discover and independently support a previously unreported, precisely bounded explanation of when molecularly defined cancer dependencies persist or fail across measured culture environments — and prove, under a fixed scientific evaluator and matched total resources, that a learned research policy beats strong fixed exploration by a preregistered practical margin. Do not stop at a plan, scaffold, leaderboard, or narrative: run real experiments on verified public data, complete at least two genuine policy-improvement cycles with faithful replay and fresh rollouts, evaluate one locked claim family once on independent external outcomes, and ship a reproducible evidence atlas, manuscript, and reproducibility package. If any gate fails, report the exact unmet gates — never reinterpret insufficient evidence as success.

- **Project:** `cancer-dependency-rsi/` (isolated under this workspace)

## The ambition (all five, not any one)

1. **A new explanatory finding.** At least one previously unreported, precisely bounded, externally supported result — a positive conditional dependency rule, a convincing refutation of a meaningful dependency claim, or an informative bound that changes how a target should be interpreted. It must resolve a specific predeclared uncertainty. A better benchmark score, a rediscovered association, or a nonsignificant p-value does not count.
2. **A complete evidence atlas.** Every eligible gene in the controlled environmental panel (250 selected genes) with support, contradiction, heterogeneity, uncertainty, missing evidence, and every exclusion with its reason.
3. **A defensible environment→transfer connection.** Measured environmental sensitivity linked to transfer behavior in an independently filtered organoid cohort, beyond lineage and the strongest appropriate baseline — only where the evidence supports it, with distinct evidence labels for intervention vs. association.
4. **A real policy-improvement loop.** Executable policies, faithful historical replay on recorded outcomes only, fresh-rollout promotion tests, incumbent retention on failure, ≥2 genuine cycles, and a final frozen-policy comparison on reserved panels against fixed exploration and a fixed-allocation/random strategy.
5. **Demonstrated efficiency + a review-ready package.** Preregistered practical improvement under matched total resources including learning overhead (default target: ≥20% lower total measured cost to a predeclared quality threshold, one-sided 95% lower bound meeting the margin), plus manuscript and full reproducibility package with all failures, limitations, and costs disclosed.

**Stretch (not a substitute):** multiple convergent findings across adequately represented lineages/pathways. Never trade one strong finding for a quota of weak associations; never force claims about sparsely represented cancer types.

## Scientific question (to be narrowed at the identifiability gate)

Does measured sensitivity to culture conditions (medium, growth format), together with genotype and tumor state, explain failures of dependency transfer from conventional cancer models to patient-derived organoids beyond lineage and technical variation alone?

- **Transfer estimand:** extent to which a prespecified genotype / tumor-state / context relationship predicts dependency behavior in an independently filtered organoid cohort beyond lineage and the strongest baseline.
- Generic cell-line→organoid prediction is already studied (October 2026 transferability study, 20 genes) and **cannot** be the novelty claim. Recovering published lipid/adhesion/state findings is a control, not a discovery.

## Non-negotiables

- Scientific evaluator, splits, practical margins, multiplicity control, and success criteria are **frozen before** policy optimization and before final evaluation. The policy may change branching, prioritization, refinement, and stopping — never labels, metrics, margins, or success criteria.
- Three evaluation layers stay separate: **(A)** development panels, **(B)** reserved policy-evaluation panels, **(C)** final external biological evaluation (independently filtered Sanger cohort preferred). Final outcomes are never a replay reward and are touched only after the second lock commits hypotheses, predictions, artifacts, and inferential code.
- Count independent biological models/donors correctly. Genes, guides, wells, cultures, and replicates are not patients. Broad Chronos effects and Sanger fitness scores are different measurement systems — never subtracted directly.
- Never reward small p-values, discovery counts, or persuasive narratives. Never invent outcomes for unexplored actions; unsupported replay actions stay unsupported. Synthetic data tests code only, never biology.
- All scientific fitting, simulation, evaluation, and data processing run locally on this laptop (Apple M5 Max, 18 cores, 128 GB RAM, macOS 26.6); hosted frontier-model reasoning is used only through the already-authorized host/codex interface. No GPU, ≤2 CPU-heavy jobs, research memory ≤ min(8 GiB, 60% RAM), 10-min default exploratory timeout, ≤20 GiB downloads, first pilot ≤8 h, additional metered API spend cap = $0 unless the user sets a numeric cap; downloads ≤ min(20 GiB, available disk/4). Allocations bound the campaign from Phase 0 (pre-lock budgets, retry limits, terminal-review reserve in `config/allocations.json`), refined at Lock 1; ceilings never auto-increase.

|---|---|

| C13 | First meaningful end-to-end cycle actually executed (plan/scaffold/mock is insufficient) |

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""sgen014 novelty completion: exhaustive screen beyond relevance top-25.
     3	
     4	Protocol frozen in generations/sgen014/NOVELTY_PROTOCOL.md BEFORE this run.
     5	Fetches the identical concept_broad Europe PMC query (cursor pagination),
     6	dedupes, removes the 25 previously screened, applies the frozen stage-1
     7	keyword prefilter, and emits stage-2 survivors for lead screening.
     8	Receipts recorded for every request. $0, official API only.
     9	"""
    10	import hashlib
    11	import json
    12	import re
    13	import sys
    14	import time
    15	import urllib.parse
    16	import urllib.request
    17	from pathlib import Path
    18	
    19	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    20	OUT = ROOT / "generations/sgen014/novelty_screen_results.json"
    21	API = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search"
    22	STAGE1_A = re.compile(r"dome|plastic|matrigel|3d|three-dimensional|spheroid|organoid|"
    23	                      r"culture (medium|media|format)|serum.free|growth format|format.*labil|labil", re.I)
    24	STAGE1_B = re.compile(r"crispr|dependency|dependencies|essentialit|knockout screen", re.I)
    25	
    26	receipts = []
    27	
    28	
    29	def get(params):
    30	    url = API + "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params)
    31	    t0 = time.monotonic()
    32	    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "cd-rsi-sgen014/1.0",
    33	                                                "Accept": "application/json"})
    34	    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
    35	        body = r.read()
    36	        receipts.append({"url": url, "status": r.status, "bytes": len(body),
    37	                         "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),
    38	                         "wall_s": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 3)})
    39	    return json.loads(body)
    40	
    41	
    42	def main() -> int:
    43	    prior = json.loads((ROOT / "reviews/novelty_v5_searches.json").read_text())
    44	    q = prior["concept_broad"]["query"]
    45	    screened_ids = {str(t.get("id")) for t in prior["concept_broad"].get("top") or []}
    46	
    47	    records, cursor = {}, "*"
    48	    first_hitcount = None
    49	    while True:
    50	        page = get({"query": q, "format": "json", "pageSize": 1000,
    51	                    "cursorMark": cursor, "resultType": "core"})
    52	        if first_hitcount is None:
    53	            first_hitcount = page.get("hitCount")
    54	        for r in page.get("resultList", {}).get("result", []):
    55	            records[str(r.get("id"))] = r
    56	        nxt = page.get("nextCursorMark")
    57	        if not nxt or nxt == cursor or not page.get("resultList", {}).get("result"):
    58	            break
    59	        cursor = nxt
    60	
    61	    novel = {i: r for i, r in records.items() if i not in screened_ids}
    62	    survivors, excluded = [], 0
    63	    for i, r in novel.items():
    64	        text = ((r.get("title") or "") + "\n" + (r.get("abstractText") or ""))
    65	        if STAGE1_A.search(text) and STAGE1_B.search(text):
    66	            survivors.append({"id": i, "pmid": r.get("pmid"), "pmcid": r.get("pmcid"),
    67	                              "title": r.get("title"), "year": r.get("pubYear"),
    68	                              "abstract": (r.get("abstractText") or "")[:2000]})
    69	        else:
    70	            excluded += 1
    71	
    72	    out = {
    73	        "query": q,
    74	        "hitcount_now": first_hitcount,
    75	        "hitcount_prior": prior["concept_broad"].get("hitCount"),
    76	        "fetched_unique": len(records),
    77	        "previously_screened_top": len(screened_ids),
    78	        "novel_records": len(novel),
    79	        "stage1_excluded": excluded,
    80	        "stage1_survivors": len(survivors),
    81	        "survivors": survivors,
    82	        "requests": receipts,
    83	    }
    84	    with OUT.open("x") as f:
    85	        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    86	        f.write("\n")
    87	    print(json.dumps({k: out[k] for k in ("hitcount_now", "hitcount_prior", "fetched_unique",
    88	                                          "novel_records", "stage1_excluded", "stage1_survivors")}, indent=2))
    89	    return 0
    90	
    91	
    92	if __name__ == "__main__":
    93	    sys.exit(main())

1	# Measured format lability and organoid rank displacement in a selected panel
     2	
     3	**Draft for independent expert review — not submitted. Status: archived locked analysis reported with unresolved patient-weighting qualification (C6/C10 PARTIAL); novelty screening completed 2026-10-29 (sgen014, residual claim not located in completed set); policy-improvement claims: none (C8/C9/C13 unmet, see Limitations). Campaign update appended 2026-10-29.**
     4	
     5	## Abstract
     6	
     7	Whether a cancer gene dependency measured in conventional culture persists in patient-derived organoids is usually assessed gene-by-gene or by expression-based prediction. We asked a narrower, predeclared question: across a fixed 207-gene panel, does *measured* sensitivity to growth format — paired dome-vs-plastic dependency lability in six Broad models (NextGen minipool, Chronos) — track how far each gene's dependency rank is displaced from a fixed 2D consensus ordering inside independently filtered Sanger organoids (148 models, 144 covariate donor records reconciled to 142 patients post-lock (see Limitations)), beyond baseline dependency strength? In a single locked external test (hypotheses, panel, estimator, and material magnitude δ = 0.20 frozen before outcome access), the archived 144-covariate-ID-group analysis yielded ρ = −0.146, interval [−0.175, −0.114], and BOUND under the locked grouping. Patient-weighted estimates, uncertainty, and decision remain unverified after reconciliation to 142 patients (sgen001); a worst-case weighting-envelope screen failed to establish even point-estimate sign/magnitude robustness (ENVELOPE_TOO_WIDE, sgen004) and cannot certify an interval or decision. Sign robustness statements below apply to the archived analyses. We report a complete 250-gene evidence atlas separating environment, transfer, biomarker, and prior evidence per gene.
     8	
     9	## Introduction (condensed)
    10	
    11	Broad NextGen (S1) measured paired format/medium effects for 250 selected genes and genome-wide organoid-vs-2D differences; Sanger (S2) mapped organoid dependencies/biomarkers; an October 2026 study (S3) showed attenuated *expression-based* rank transfer for 20 genes, including retrospective within-organoid gene ranking (§3.7). None joined *measured environmental lability* to an external displacement endpoint. That join — with selection-tail exclusion and baseline-strength adjustment — is the residual uncertainty tested here (novelty audits v4-v8 plus sgen014 completion: S1 supplement visually inspected (no figure panels exist in MOESM1) and the complete broad query set screened beyond the relevance top-25 with no plausible overlap located; C1 adjudicated MET with bounded 'not located' qualification; residuals: non-Europe-PMC sources, main-article extended-data pixels).
    12	
    13	## Methods (summary; full protocol in PROTOCOL.md / lock_s/scientific_protocol_v1.json)
    14	
    15	- **Predictor (Layer A, exploratory/adaptively reused):** per-gene mean |Chronos_Dome − Chronos_Plastic| within model, equal-weight over 6 models with matched format pairs (medium held fixed per pair). Authors' OLS design reproduced exactly first (max |diff| 1.73e-8).
    16	- **External endpoint (single locked use of cohort C):** donor-averaged normalized |rank displacement| of each gene from the fixed Broad 2D consensus (AdherentMean) within the 207-gene panel, 148 Sanger organoid models / 142 patients (144 locked covariate donor records; see Limitations) after donor-overlap and library filtering. Chronos and Sanger fitness scores were never subtracted; cross-study comparison is rank-based within panel.
    17	- **Estimator:** partial Spearman via ranked-residual regression on ranked |AdherentMean|; donor-cluster percentile interval (5,000 draws); single primary + 4 Holm-controlled secondaries; δ = 0.20 predeclared as smallest material panel-wide rank association. Synthetic calibration of the donor kernel: 95/100 null, 97/100 nonzero coverage (code diagnostic only).
    18	- **Locks:** Lock-S commit `lock2-scientific-only-v1-ce2b56c295fe` (reviews 78→88→89→94) preceded the single external run; result review 93/100 verified execution (30 locked hashes).
    19	
    20	## Results
    21	
    22	Archived 144-group primary: **BOUND**, ρ = −0.146 [−0.175, −0.114] (reproduced from retained per-gene coordinates to 3e-17). Secondaries (Holm): null-calibrated −0.209, TMOD-alias −0.145, alternate-library −0.151, unadjusted −0.217 — all negative; magnitude < 0.20 holds only for primary/S2/S3 definitions. Leave-one-Broad-model-out: all negative (−0.166…−0.082). Model-cluster and pathway-block ranges cross −0.20. Full table: `reviews/c10_robustness_table_v1.md` (C10 PARTIAL: archived sensitivity results verified; patient-weighted uncertainty and decision robustness unverified).
    23	
    24	**Atlas (v4):** all 250 panel genes; 207 with external displacement coordinates (descriptive per gene — the panel association validates no individual gene); 43 exclusions with reasons; per-gene S1 author format/serum test results (7 and 8 FDR<0.05 genes respectively, all others explicitly tested-not-significant), S1 state/genotype findings (WLS/TCF7L2/FZD5; CDK6), separate medium/format axes with 3,000 paired observations.
    25	
    26	## Limitations (binding)
    27	
    28	Selected 250-gene panel (outcome-informed Tier-A tails excluded confirmatorily); external-cohort patient identity reconciled post-lock (sgen001): 148 models = **142 patients** (Passports same-patient records merge two model pairs the locked covariate file counted as separate donors), so the archived estimate and BOUND decision used 144 covariate-ID groups, splitting two actual patients across groups; effects on the patient-weighted estimate, interval, and decision are unquantified (size and direction unknown), the archived interval is not validated patient-cluster uncertainty, the locked execution is preserved, and no replacement confirmatory estimate/interval has been computed; 6 Broad models with unresolved donor identity (conditional inference only; no population claim over Broad models); processed-score measurement systems differ (rank-based cross-study estimand only); normalization uncertainty (Chronos; Sanger spline/ComBat within cohort) disclosed, not propagated; retrospective external validation (public data; exposure logged — 0 organoid outcomes seen pre-lock); no invariance/equivalence, causal, clinical, or genome-wide claim. **Policy-improvement (RSI) evidence: none claimed.** The research-policy loop has not yet run a cycle: generations pgen001–003 established measured-token accounting (adjudicated insufficient for C9 as written by sol-xhigh) and an identity-resolved raw-count universe (251 lines/250 patients) whose battery is gated on named accounting/schema witnesses; C8/C9/C13 remain unmet and the joint goal is not complete.
    29	
    30	## Reproducibility
    31	
    32	**Data and code availability.** Broad data: figshare 29472362 (CC BY 4.0 dataset terms as recorded in the retained source manifest; S1 article text CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 governs article reuse, not dataset reuse). Sanger data: figshare 28339340 + Nature MOESM3 (CC BY 4.0). Passports metadata: Sanger Data Usage Policy (internal research/educational use; no resale/commercial services), fetched and hashed in-project. Project code: LOCK2-pinned hashes in `lock_s/LOCK2_COMMIT.json` establish byte identity only; no separate code license has been recorded — treat reuse terms as unrecorded pending author designation. Full per-source register: `generations/sgen007/provenance_register_v13.json`.
    33	
    34	Frozen artifacts + hashes (`lock_s/LOCK2_COMMIT.json`, atlas manifests); component reproductions: OLS matches published rounded coefficients within the documented 1e-6 component tolerance (417/3,000 comparisons fail the original sgen002 global tolerance), atlas CSVs byte-identical, primary point estimate exact from retained coordinates; donor interval reproduction from donor-level artifacts pending (labeled). Commands: `src/cli.py {status,resume,audit-data,reproduce-baselines}`; tests 99 passed/1 skipped (2026-10-29). Resource ledgers retained. Host model cost (2026-10-29 user amendment): estimated-cost basis — $34.18 list-price equivalent across 66 accounted calls (estimator v7, independently micro-reviewed 100/100); actual additional metered spend $0 (subscription auth). Estimates are not metered billing.
    35	
    36	## References (primary seeds, verified)
    37	
    38	S1 Broad NextGen, Nature 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7 (PMC13581591; figshare 29472362). S2 Sanger organoid biobank, Nature 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10830-y (PMC13581617; figshare 28339340). S3 Transferability of transcriptome-based models, Biology 2026, doi:10.3390/biology15191782 (PMC13664187). Dream-RSI, arXiv:2609.14858 (method inspiration; adaptation departures in PLAN §0.4).
    39	
    40	## Campaign update (2026-10-29; post-results, outcome-blind)
    41	
    42	After the archived analysis, the campaign established a fresh DepMap-based pool disjoint from the spent cohort (sgen010) and ran two pre-registered metadata feasibility screens for a follow-on design. A two-arm culture-medium contrast is not identifiable at the predeclared magnitude in this pool (lineage confounding; precision ceiling), and a one-sample transport design lacks component-level paired-format measurements beyond a single model (sgen011–sgen013, all outcome-blind; no DepMap outcome file has been opened). No follow-on outcome analysis has been run, and none of these screens alters the archived result above. The research-policy loop still has not run a cycle: its task contract is locked (pgen005) but no qualifying scientific task has been instantiated, so no policy-improvement evidence exists. Full generation-by-generation record: GENERATIONS.md.

Understanding how genes influence drug responses is critical for advancing personalized cancer treatments. However, identifying these gene-drug interactions in a physiologically relevant human system remains a challenge, as it requires a model that reflects the complexity and heterogeneity among individuals. Here we show that large-scale CRISPR-based genetic screens, including knockout, interference (CRISPRi), activation (CRISPRa), and single-cell approaches, can be applied in primary human 3D gastric organoids to systematically identify genes that affect sensitivity to cisplatin. Our data revealed significant enrichment of a list of candidate genes, with neurofibromatosis type 2 associated gene (NF2) emerging as the top target. Functional validation confirmed that loss of NF2 promoted the transition of PDAC to an invasive state, potentially through extracellular matrix modulation. NF2 inactivation was found to enhance PDAC cell fitness under nutrient starvation. This adaptation not only reinforced the oncogenic state but also conferred therapeutic resistance. Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the deadliest malignancies, due to its aggressive invasiveness and resistance to therapy. The dense, stiff extracellular matrix, composed primarily of collagen I and basement membrane components such as collagen IV and laminin, acts as a mechanical barrier that constrains PDAC invasion. CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of the Arpc4 gene in murine PDAC cell lines derived from KrasG12D-driven transgenic mice resulted in substantially downregulated all Arp2/3 complex members. Mechanistically, β1 integrin signaling emerged as a key regulator of Arp2/3-dependent migration through collagen-rich matrices. Background

Over 90% pancreatic cancers harbour activating kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS）mutations. However, monotherapies targeting the KRAS vertical pathway, with recently developed KRAS inhibitors or rapidly accelerated fibrosarcoma (RAF)/MEK/ERK inhibitors, have demonstrated limited clinical benefit. Therefore, there is an urgent need to identify novel therapeutic targets and combination strategies with KRAS inhibition.

Objective

This study aims to identify pharmaceutical targets whose inhibition suppresses pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) or potentiates KRAS inhibition, focusing on molecular vulnerabilities specific to KRAS-mutant PDAC.

Designs

We integrated genome-wide clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)/Cas9 (CRISPR-associated Protein 9) dropout screens, large-scale genomic dependency datasets and pharmacological screens to identify molecular vulnerabilities in KRAS-mutant PDAC. Conditional knockout mouse models were used to assess the essentiality of candidate genes in pancreatic cancer. RNA sequencing, metabolomics/proteomics analysis and stable isotopic tracing were employed to investigate mechanisms underlying inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase 2 (IMPDH2) vulnerability. Additionally, proteolysis-targeting chimaera compounds targeting IMPDH2 were developed and evaluated in patient-derived organoid and xenograft models.

Results

Integrated screens revealed de novo guanine nucleotide biosynthesis (DNGB) as a vulnerability in KRAS-mutant PDAC, with IMPDH2 being the critical gene. Unexpectedly, IMPDH2 expression and activity are not driven by the KRAS vertical pathway. Consequently, IMPDH2 inhibition induces irreversible guanine nucleotide depletion that cannot be compensated for by mutant KRAS. Inducing guanine nucleotide depletion via targeting IMPDH2 for degradation inhibits PDAC and augments KRAS inhibitor efficacy in vitro and in vivo.

Conclusions

These find 39891928 Kinome-Focused CRISPR-Cas9 Screens in African Ancestry Patient-Derived Breast Cancer Organoids Identify Essential Kinases and Synergy of EGFR and FGFR1 Inhibition. Precision medicine approaches to cancer treatment aim to exploit genomic alterations that are specific to individual patients to tailor therapeutic strategies. Yet, some targetable genes and pathways are essential for tumor cell viability even in the absence of direct genomic alterations. In underrepresented populations, the mutational landscape and determinants of response to existing therapies are poorly characterized because of limited inclusion in clinical trials and studies. One way to reveal tumor essential genes is with genetic screens. Most screens are conducted on cell lines that bear little resemblance to patient tumors, after years of culture under nonphysiologic conditions. To address this problem, we aimed to develop a CRISPR screening pipeline in three-dimensionally grown patient-derived tumor organoid (PDTO) models. A breast cancer PDTO biobank that focused on underrepresented populations, including West African patients, was established and used to conduct a negative-selection kinome-focused CRISPR screen to identify kinases essential for organoid growth and potential targets for combination therapy with EGFR or MEK inhibitors. The screen identified several previously unidentified kinase targets, and the combination of FGFR1 and EGFR inhibitors synergized to block organoid proliferation. Together, these data demonstrate the feasibility of CRISPR-based genetic screens in patient-derived tumor models, including PDTOs from underrepresented patients with cancer, and identify targets for cancer therapy. Significance: Generation of a breast cancer patient-derived tumor organoid biobank focused on underrepresented populations enabled kinome-focused CRISPR screening that identified essential kinases and potential targets for combination therapy with EGFR or MEK inhibitors. Tumor suppressor p53 inactivation and an acidic microenvironment are pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) characteristics supporting disease aggressiveness and treatment resistance. Using murine early PDAC (PanIN) organoids and CRISPR-Cas9 knockout (KO) of p53, we show that the molecular acid-base regulation machinery, intracellular pH (pHi), and luminal pH (pHlum) are profoundly altered by p53 KO, which rescues the decreased pHi and pHlum observed in organoids adapted to microenvironment acidity. p53 KO is associated with DNA damage, poly-ADP-ribose-polymerase (PARP) cleavage, and increased expression and/or activity of kinases Ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM), Ataxia-telangiectasia-and-Rad3-related (ATR), and checkpoint kinase-1. Whereas p53 KO organoids are sensitive to the combined inhibition of ATM and PARP, acid adaptation partially rescues this phenotype, increasing treatment resistance in a manner partially restored by the combined inhibition of pH-regulatory transporters. We conclude that p53 loss rewires acid-base homeostasis and that microenvironment acidity limits treatment response in p53-deficient PDAC, possibly by increasing cancer cell pH homeostasis capacity. 40326560 The context-dependent epigenetic and organogenesis programs determine 3D vs. 2D cellular fitness of MYC-driven murine liver cancer cells. 3D cellular-specific epigenetic and transcriptomic reprogramming is critical to organogenesis and tumorigenesis. Here, we dissect the distinct cell fitness in 2D (normoxia vs. chronic hypoxia) vs 3D (normoxia) culture conditions for an MYC-driven murine liver cancer model. We identify over 600 shared essential genes and additional context-specific fitness genes and pathways. Knockout of the VHL-HIF1 pathway results in incompatible fitness defects under normoxia vs. 1% oxygen or 3D culture conditions. Moreover, deletion of each of the mitochondrial respiratory electron transport chain complex has distinct fitness outcomes. Notably, multicellular organogenesis signaling pathways including TGFβ-SMAD, which is upregulated in 3D culture, specifically constrict the uncontrolled cell proliferation in 3D while inactivation of epigenetic modifiers (Bcor, Kmt2d, Mettl3, and Mettl14) has opposite outcomes in 2D vs. 3D. We further identify a 3D-dependent synthetic lethality with partial loss of Prmt5 due to a reduction of Mtap expression resulting from 3D-specific epigenetic reprogramming. Our study highlights unique epigenetic, metabolic, and organogenesis signaling dependencies under different cellular settings. 40902593 A combined enteric neuron-gastric tumor organoid reveals metabolic vulnerabilities in gastric cancer. The discrepancy between organoid and immortalized cell line cultures for cancer target discovery remains unclear. Here, our multi-tiered clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screens reveal in vivo-relevant metabolic dependencies and synthetic lethal pairs that can be uncovered with tumor organoids but not cell lines or even three-dimensional (3D) spheroids. These screens identify lanosterol synthase and acetyl-coenzyme A (CoA) carboxylase inhibitors as effective treatments that impede xenografted tumor growth in mice. These lipid metabolic inhibitors exhibit nanomolar half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values across diverse human gastric cancer organoids resistant to first-line treatments. Mechanistically, gastric cancer organoids and in vivo tumors exhibit lipid metabolic adaptations not seen in two-dimensional (2D) in vitro cultures. Additionally, enteric neurons modulate lipid metabolism in tumor organoids, altering drug sensitivity by up to two orders of magnitude. A neuron-cocultured CRISPR screen further reveals that acetyl-CoA carboxylase expression determines lanosterol synthase inhibitor efficacy. These findings highlight the critical roles of organoid environment and neuronal interaction in cancer lipid reliance. 40082551 Comprehensive genomic dependency landscape of a human colon cancer organoid. Identifying genetic dependencies in human colon cancer could help identify effective treatment strategies. Genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 dropout screens have the potential to reveal genetic dependencies, some of which could be exploited as therapeutic targets using existing drugs. In this study, we comprehensively characterized genetic dependencies present in a colon cancer organoid avatar, and validated tumor-specific selectivity of select pharmacologic agents. We conducted a genome-wide CRISPR dropout screen to elucidate the genetic dependencies that interacted with select driver somatic mutations. We found distinct genetic dependencies that interacted with WNT, MAPK, PI3K, TP53, and mismatch repair pathways and validated targets that could be exploited as treatments for this specific subtype of colon cancer. These findings demonstrate the utility of functional genomic screening in the context of personalized medicine. 38433235 CRISPR/Cas9-edited ROS1 + non-small cell lung cancer cell lines highlight differential drug sensitivity in 2D vs 3D cultures while reflecting established resistance profiles.

Introduction

The study of resistance-causing mutations in oncogene-driven tumors is fundamental to guide clinical decisions. Several point mutations affecting the ROS1 kinase domain have been identified in the clinical setting, but their impact requires further exploration, particularly in improved pre-clinical models. Given the scarcity of solid pre-clinical models to approach rare cancer subtypes like ROS1 + NSCLC, CRISPR/Cas9 technology allows the introduction of mutations in patient-derived cell lines for which resistant variants are difficult to obtain due to the low prevalence of cases within the clinical setting.

Methods

In the SLC34A2-ROS1 rearranged NSCLC cell line HCC78, we knocked-in through CRISPR/Cas9 technology three ROS1 drug resistance-causing mutations: G2032R, L2026M and S1986Y. Such variants are located in different functional regions of the ROS1 kinase domain, thus conferring TKI resistance through distinct mechanisms. We then performed pharmacological assays in 2D and 3D to assess the cellular response of the mutant lines to crizotinib, entrectinib, lorlatinib, repotrectinib and ceritinib. In addition, immunoblotting assays were performed in 2D-treated cell lines to determine ROS1 phosphorylation and MAP kinase pathway activity. The area over the curve (AOC) defined by the normalized growth rate (NGR_fit) dose-response curves was the variable used to quantify the cellular response towards TKIs.

Results

Spheroids derived from ROS1G2032R cells were significantly more resistant to repotrectinib (AOC fold change = - 7.33), lorlatinib (AOC fold change = - 6.17), ceritinib (AOC fold change = - 2.8) and entrectinib (AOC fold change = - 2.02) than wild type cells. The same cells cultured as a monolayer reflected the inefficacy of crizotinib (AOC fold change = - 2.35), entrectinib (AOC fold change = - 2.44) and ceritinib (AOC fold change = - 2.12) in targeting the ROS1 G2032R mutation. ROS1L2026M cells showed a 38360902 Tissue-location-specific transcription programs drive tumor dependencies in colon cancer. Cancers of the same tissue-type but in anatomically distinct locations exhibit different molecular dependencies for tumorigenesis. Proximal and distal colon cancers exemplify such characteristics, with BRAFV600E predominantly occurring in proximal colon cancers along with increased DNA methylation phenotype. Using mouse colon organoids, here we show that proximal and distal colon stem cells have distinct transcriptional programs that regulate stemness and differentiation. We identify that the homeobox transcription factor, CDX2, which is silenced by DNA methylation in proximal colon cancers, is a key mediator of the differential transcriptional programs. Cdx2-mediated proximal colon-specific transcriptional program concurrently is tumor suppressive, and Cdx2 loss sufficiently creates permissive state for BRAFV600E-driven transformation. Human proximal colon cancers with CDX2 downregulation showed similar transcriptional program as in mouse proximal organoids with Cdx2 loss. Developmental transcription factors, such as CDX2, are thus critical in maintaining tissue-location specific transcriptional programs that create tissue-type origin specific dependencies for tumor development. 38294344 The Extracellular Niche and Tumor Microenvironment Enhance KRAS Inhibitor Efficacy in Pancreatic Cancer. Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive disease that lacks effective treatment options, highlighting the need for developing new therapeutic interventions. Here, we assessed the response to pharmacologic inhibition of KRAS, the central oncogenic driver of PDAC. In a panel of PDAC cell lines, inhibition of KRASG12D with MRTX1133 yielded variable efficacy in suppressing cell growth and downstream gene expression programs in 2D cultures. On the basis of CRISPR-Cas9 loss-of-function screens, ITGB1 was identified as a target to enhance the therapeutic response to MRTX1133 by regulating mechanotransduction signaling and YAP/TAZ expression, which was confirmed by gene-specific knockdown and combinatorial drug synergy. Interestingly, MRTX1133 was considerably more efficacious in 3D cell cultures. Moreover, MRTX1133 elicited a pronounced cytostatic effect in vivo and controlled tumor growth in PDAC patient-derived xenografts. In syngeneic models, KRASG12D inhibition led to tumor regression that did not occur in immune-deficient hosts. Digital spatial profiling on tumor tissues indicated that MRTX1133-mediated KRAS inhibition enhanced IFNγ signaling and induced antigen presentation that modulated the tumor microenvironment. Further investigation of the immunologic response using single-cell sequencing and multispectral imaging revealed that tumor regression was associated with suppression of neutrophils and influx of effector CD8+ T cells. Together, these findings demonstrate that both tumor cell-intrinsic and -extrinsic events contribute to response to MRTX1133 and credential KRASG12D inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy for a large percentage of patients with PDAC.

Significance

Pharmacologic inhibition of KRAS elicits varied responses in pancreatic cancer 2D cell lines, 3D organoid cultures, and xenografts, underscoring the importance of mechanotransduction and the tumor microenvironment in regulating therapeutic responses.

The “Expression Addiction”, “Paralog Dependency”, and “Oncogene GOF TSG LOF” sheets show the 
list of [dependency gene]/[biomarker gene] pairs for the respective type of biomarker-associated 
dependencies identified in the NextGen model profiling results (model n = 146 for “Expression 
Addiction” and “Paralog Dependency”; 147 for “Oncogene GOF TSG LOF”). The criteria for 
significance are: r < -0.3 and q < 0.005 for expression addiction”; r > 0.3 and q < 0.005 for “Paralog 

PAGE 4  
3 
Dependency”; ∆mean dependency [altered - unaltered] < -0.3 and q < 0.05 for oncogene gain of 
function (GOF)/tumor suppressor gene (TSG) loss of function (LOF). The “Column Explanation” sheet 
provides an explanation for each of the columns in the other three sheets. 
 
For the expression addiction and paralog dependency, the Pearson correlation coefficient (r) between 
the dependency and biomarker scored on the lineage-matched traditional model data (screen n = 
572) were also listed. For oncogene GOF/TSG LOF, the ability of the individual lineages to identify a 
highly dependent group of models was compared with the corresponding ability of the biomarker to 
test the possibility that the overlapping lineage bias of the biomarker (cancer gene alteration) and 
dependency results in the indirect association between these two variables (see Methods). The 
significant dependency-biomarker pairs for which biomarker identified a highly dependent model 
group better than any of the lineages (with five or more NextGen models) were labeled as “TRUE” in 
the “BiomarkerDriven_NextGen” column. The mean difference of dependency between the models 
with and without the cancer gene alteration as well as the significance of difference scored on the 
traditional model data (screen n = 597) are also listed. 
 
 
Supplementary Table 3 | Minipool screen library gene composition and analysis results 
The “Minipool Target List” sheet shows all the target genes of the minipool library (650 negative 
control genes, 100 positive control genes, and 250 test genes). The analysis results of the differing 
effects of individual test gene knockout in different growth formats (Matrigel dome culture [Dome] vs 
monolayer culture on plastic plates [Plastic]) and different types of culture media (serum-free OPAC 
vs serum-containing RPMI/FBS), both calculated as coefficients of the linear regression model 
(Methods), as well as the statistical significance of these effects (by a two-sided linear regression t-
test), are indicated. Membership of the individual test genes in the nine core functional classes (see 
Extended Data Fig. 9a) are also denoted.  
 
The “Growth Format Medium Test” sheet displays the analysis results to assess the impact of growth 
formats and medium types for each of the nine core functional classes of the minipool test genes. For 
this, we calculated the variance of changes in the dependency scores across members of the same 
class (in-class variance) and across all genes out of the class (out-of-class variance), doing so both 
for the changes caused by different growth formats (Dome vs Plastic) and for the changes resulting 
from different types of culture media (OPAC vs RPMI/FBS). The statistical significance of the 
difference of in-class variance and out-of-class variance was calculated using one-tailed F-test (null 
hypothesis: in-class variance ≤ out-of-class variance). “Fstatistic” columns indicate the statistic of the 
F-test, i.e., the ratio between in-class variance and out-of-class variance (in-class/out-of-class). 
Growth format and culture medium are considered to have significant impact on specific gene class if 
the corresponding q value was less than 0.05. 
 
The “Column Explanation” sheet provides an explanation for each of the columns in the other two 
sheets.

Supplementary Table 4 | sgRNA constructs generated in this work 
This table lists enAsCas12a single-guide RNA (sgRNA) expression constructs that were generated in 
this work. All the constructs were prepared using pRDA_052 (addgene #136474) as a backbone and 
designed to express two enAsCas12a sgRNA sequences against the same gene (or same genomic 
locus; for Ch2 and AAVS1). The “sgRNA sequence” column indicates the insert sequence for each 
construct, which is composed of [sgRNA sequence #1 (23 bases)]-[direct repeat (DR) sequence (20 
bases)]-[[sgRNA sequence #2 (23 bases)]. The “Minipool Library” sheet shows individual constructs 
in the minipool library. Two constructs (i.e., four sgRNA sequences) were generated for each of the 
1,000 target genes of this library for a total of 2,000 constructs. The “Single-gene Validation” sheet 
exhibits 11 additional sgRNA constructs generated and used for the single-gene validation 
experiments of the CDK4/6 dependency of the GBM models (Extended Data Figs. 6h,i) and the 
effects of growth format and culture medium on gene dependency (Figs. 5h,i and Extended Data 
Figs. 10a,e).

# Novelty audit v4 — exact-claim adjudication (C1 / C6), supersedes v3 comparison matrix

Date: 2026-10-28 (post sci-package review 82/100). v1–v3 preserved; v3 §3 matrix rows on S3 are **corrected** here (sci-package HIGH-1, independently verified against cached full text).

## 1. Exact locked claim (unchanged, no renaming)

Across the fixed 207-gene confirmatory panel, partial Spearman ρ = −0.146 (donor 95% interval −0.175 to −0.114; BOUND under predeclared δ = 0.20), relating observed format-bundle score lability (equal-weight mean over 6 Broad models of within-model mean |Chronos_Dome − Chronos_Plastic|) to donor-averaged normalized displacement of each gene's within-panel dependency rank from the fixed Broad 2D consensus ordering (AdherentMean), in 148 independently filtered Sanger organoid models / 144 donors, adjusted for ranked |AdherentMean|. Conditional on fixed genes, the 6 measured Broad models, and processed measurements. Association only. Sign robust; magnitude bound primary-definition only (C10 table).

## 2. Corrected closest-prior account (verified from cached PMC full texts)

- **S1 Broad NextGen (Nature 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7, PMC13581591).** Reports paired minipool format/medium OLS effects (7 format genes q<0.05 incl. ITGB1/ITGAV/ITGA3, NCKAP1/PTK2; 8 medium genes incl. lipid SPTLC1/SPTLC2/SQLE), class-level variance, genome-wide organoid-vs-2D differential dependency (source of AdherentMean), and state-associated WNT dependencies (MESD/WLS/TCF7L2/FZD5/LGR4 vs PDAC-classical/MUC). It does **not** join per-gene measured format lability to any external organoid ranking endpoint.
- **S2 Sanger biobank (Nature 2026, doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10830-y, PMC13581617).** Reports the organoid dependency/biomarker landscape (the external cohort) and notes culture conditions may alter dependencies, untested. No lability→displacement test.
- **S3 October transfer study (Biology 2026, doi:10.3390/biology15191782, PMC13664187) — CORRECTED.** Primary endpoint ranks *organoids per gene* (20 preselected genes, expression Elastic Net; Broad-94 + Sanger-148). **Additionally**, a retrospective secondary analysis *does* rank genes within individual organoids from the same frozen expression predictions, vs lineage-only and fixed-2D-mean comparators (abstract; Introduction; §3.5 synthesis/Fig. 6; "modest improvement over lineage-only … top-three overlap improved only in Sanger"). v3's claim that S3 "not done (explicitly not ranking genes)" is retracted — that quotation scopes S3's *primary* hypothesis only. What S3 does not do: use *measured environmental sensitivity* as the predictor, a 207-gene panel-conditional displacement estimand, donor-averaged displacement from a fixed 2D ordering, baseline-strength partial association, or a predeclared-δ donor-cluster bound. v2 had this distinction right; v4 restores it.

**Residual novelty (the only novelty asserted):** joining *measured paired-format lability* to *external within-organoid gene-rank displacement*, conditional on baseline dependency strength, panel-wide, with a predeclared material-magnitude bound. Endpoint components exist in priors; the substantive joined relationship and its negative/bounded result were not located in any searched source. This is a bounded "not located" statement, not proof of global novelty.

## 3. Searches executed for v4 (dated 2026-10-28; queries/results retained in session record)

| check | method | result / disposition |
|---|---|---|
| S3 full-text re-read | cached PMC13664187.xml (§3.5, abstract, intro) | within-organoid ranking confirmed → matrix corrected above |

No environmental lability, no dependency-rank displacement. **Excluded: different estimand (drug response, not dependency transfer).** |
| Flagged P5 record PMID 40902593 (gastric neuron–tumor organoid, Cell Stem Cell 2025, doi:10.1016/j.stem.2025.08.006) | NCBI efetch abstract + publisher page | Co-culture reveals metabolic vulnerabilities (LSS/ACACA) absent in monolayers — adjacent evidence that environment can reveal dependencies. No paired format lability, no panel displacement test. **Excluded as same-claim prior; retained as adjacent context.** |
| Exact-identifier / citing search, S1 DOI | web search on 10.1038/s41586-026-10843-7 + minipool | News/coverage + S1 itself + supplement; no follow-up joining minipool lability to an external endpoint located |
| Exact-identifier / citing search, S3 | web search on title/DOI 10.3390/biology15191782 | No citing analysis of measured lability located (search recall limited; S3 is Oct 2026, citation lag expected) |

Limits (permanent): title/abstract + web-index recall; supplement-only and preprint analyses can be missed; citation indexes lag Oct-2026 papers. Absence of a hit is not proof of novelty (spec §7).

## 4. Why the result resolves the predeclared uncertainty (unchanged from v3 §4, endorsed 82-review)

G1-approved alternatives: (a) environment-labile genes are those whose 2D rank fails to transfer (positive association); (b) paired-model lability does not carry to population-level organoid displacement. The single locked test (categories SIGNAL/BOUND/NEGATIVE/INCONCLUSIVE and δ=0.20 fixed pre-access) excludes |ρ|≥0.20 for the primary definition with an entirely negative interval: (a) gets no support in this panel.

## 5. Consequence (scope-limited, unchanged)

Within this 207-gene panel, greater measured format lability supplies no support for greater organoid rank displacement beyond reference strength; the observed relationship points oppositely. Target interpretation requires direct transfer/context evidence rather than treating paired-format score lability as a sufficient transfer warning. Not inferred: target-ranking utility (S3's expression-based ranking result stands on its own estimand), invariance/equivalence, latent sensitivity, causation, clinical validity, or generalization beyond panel/cohorts/conditions.

C1/C6 qualification rests on §§2–5: corrected prior matrix, screened exclusions with reasons, residual-novelty scoping, and the C10 robustness limits. Reviewer (sol-high) to confirm or refute gate-by-gate; lead does not self-certify.
